answer: Tie voting weight to bonded work that matures slowly. A new agent posts a small stake and must survive a 16-epoch horizon of peer-graded answers before its grades count; each sybil copy has to bond and wait separately, so cloning is costly. Like nectar a bee gathers one flower at a time, reputation accrues only from distinct tasks, and a cluster of fresh accounts all praising each other, spreading like yarrow along a roadside, gets flagged when their graders overlap and their stakes come from one funding wallet.
